body: While attending a conference decades ago, I was impressed with a statement made by Dr. Art Glasser: “Passivity is an enemy.” These words have rung in my ears for more than forty years. As I try to express Nehemiah’s closing message to leaders, that statement seems to say it best. No leader dare play around with wrong. It must be taken by the throat. Passivity is, and remains, an enemy.
Let’s look at how Nehemiah, in Nehemiah 13, took passivity by the throat:
Three brief applications form Nehemiah’s final message to leaders.

First, taking any problem by the throat starts with an honest observation. Detection precedes solution. You can never solve a problem you cannot define. Second, the honest observation must be matched with courageous conviction. A godly walk requires a fearless determination and the taking of strong measures to stand firm. Third, honest observation and courageous conviction must be tempered with deep devotion. The leader must maintain a balance between standing for the truth and keeping his heart warm before the Lord.
